23 The table lists possible orders of magnitude of the wavelengths of some of the principal radiations
of the electromagnetic spectrum.
Which row shows the correct orders of magnitude of the wavelengths?
wavelength / m
microwaves
infra-red
ultraviolet
X-rays
A
10–6
10–10
10–12
10–14
B
10–4
10–8
10–10
10–12
C
10–2
10–6
10–8
10–10
D
102
10–4
10–6
10–8

hints: Notice the columns run from microwaves on the left to X-rays on the right, so the wavelength in $\text{m}$ must get smaller from left to right.
Recall the middle of the spectrum with infra-red near $10^{-6}$ $\text{m}$ and ultraviolet near $10^{-8}$ $\text{m}$, just beyond visible light at about $10^{-7}$ $\text{m}$.
Check the ends against known anchors: microwaves near $10^{-2}$ $\text{m}$ and X-rays near $10^{-10}$ $\text{m}$, then find the row that matches all four.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: four orders of magnitude in $\text{m}$ for microwaves, infra-red, ultraviolet and X-rays in each row A to D.
State the governing order: in the electromagnetic spectrum wavelength decreases from radio to gamma, so microwaves > infra-red > ultraviolet > X-rays.
Recall typical values: microwaves about $10^{-3}$ to $10^{-1}$ $\text{m}$, infra-red about $10^{-6}$ $\text{m}$, ultraviolet about $10^{-8}$ $\text{m}$, and X-rays about $10^{-10}$ $\text{m}$.
Compare each row: rows A and B make microwaves and infra-red too short, and row D makes microwaves $10^{2}$ $\text{m}$ which is too long for microwaves.
Only the row with $10^{-2}$ $\text{m}$, $10^{-6}$ $\text{m}$, $10^{-8}$ $\text{m}$ and $10^{-10}$ $\text{m}$ fits all four regions in the correct decreasing order. This is option C.

A.explanation: All values are far too small, with microwaves at $10^{-6}$ $\text{m}$ instead of about $10^{-2}$ $\text{m}$ and X-rays at $10^{-14}$ $\text{m}$.

B.explanation: Each wavelength is about two orders too small, giving infra-red as $10^{-8}$ $\text{m}$ and X-rays as $10^{-12}$ $\text{m}$.

C.explanation: Wavelength decreases correctly from microwaves $10^{-2}$ $\text{m}$ to X-rays $10^{-10}$ $\text{m}$ via infra-red and ultraviolet.

D.explanation: Each wavelength is far too large, with microwaves at $10^{2}$ $\text{m}$ which is in the radio wave region.
